Section 3.  Additional Rent; Operating Expenses.  In addition to Base Rent, Tenant shall pay as additional rent (“Additional Rent”) Tenant’s proportionate share (based on the square footage of the Leased Premises relative to the total leasable square footage of the building) of

Landlord’s reasonable, actual, and customary costs of: (a) real estate taxes and assessments in accordance with Article VI; (b) commercially reasonable insurance premiums for the insurance Landlord is required to maintain under Article XII; and (c) reasonable costs of operating, maintaining, and repairing common areas serving the building, including shared parking areas (collectively,

Landlord’s reasonable costs of owning, operating, maintaining, repairing, replacing, managing, and insuring the building and common areas, including real estate taxes and assessments; insurance premiums; utilities; security; refuse and snow removal; common-area maintenance and repair; and a management fee equal to three percent (3%) of gross rents (collectively,
“Operating Expenses”).

Operating Expenses shall exclude, in all cases, capital expenditures, reserves, depreciation, debt service, leasing commissions, and costs of a capital nature except as expressly permitted under Article VIII.

Operating Expenses shall also include capital expenditures required by laws enacted after the date of this Lease or reasonably intended to reduce Operating Expenses, in each case amortized over the item’s useful life with interest at the rate reasonably charged by Landlord’s lender. Costs attributable solely to Tenant’s clinical operations, including regulated medical waste, supplemental security or janitorial service, and after-hours HVAC, shall be billed directly to Tenant and shall not be subject to the cap in Section 4.

Landlord shall provide Tenant with an annual estimate of Additional Rent, payable in equal monthly installments, together with an annual reconciliation against actual, invoiced costs within ninety (90) days after the end of each calendar year, accompanied by reasonably detailed supporting documentation, and Tenant shall have the right to audit Landlord’s books and records relating to Operating Expenses upon reasonable prior notice, at Tenant’s expense unless such audit reveals an overstatement of Operating Expenses in excess of three percent (3%), in which case Landlord shall bear the reasonable cost of the audit and promptly refund the overstated amount.

Landlord shall provide an annual estimate and reconciliation with reasonably detailed supporting documentation. Tenant may audit Operating Expenses once per calendar year, at Tenant’s cost, by a qualified auditor not compensated on a contingency basis, upon written notice given within ninety (90) days after receipt of the reconciliation; Landlord shall reimburse reasonable audit costs only if the audit establishes an overstatement exceeding five percent (5%).

Section 4.  Landlord’s Failure to Maintain.

If Landlord fails to commence necessary repairs to a building system described in Section 1 of this Article VIII within five (5) business days after written notice from Tenant (or immediately in the case of an emergency affecting patient safety or Tenant’s ability to operate), and such failure materially interferes with Tenant’s ability to safely treat patients, Tenant may, without waiving any other remedy, perform such repairs itself and deduct the reasonable, documented cost thereof, together with interest at the rate set forth in Article XV, from the next installment(s) of Base Rent due under this Lease.

If Landlord fails to commence necessary repairs after telephonic and written notice from Tenant of an emergency posing an imminent threat to patient safety or rendering the Leased Premises unusable, Tenant may, using contractors approved by Landlord in advance, perform only the repairs reasonably necessary to address the emergency. Landlord shall reimburse Tenant’s documented, reasonable costs within thirty (30) days or dispute them in writing, and any dispute shall be resolved by expedited arbitration. Tenant’s remedy for nonpayment shall be a claim and not a deduction or offset against rent.
